scope: Original flowers, climbers and kitchen crops; garden-scale interpretations preserving catalogue placement envelopes

references.features: Basal foliage rosette and one-sided pendant foxglove racemes with spotted throats.
Three upright standards and three drooping bearded falls, basal sword leaves.
Broad cupped overlapping petals on leafy herbaceous stems.
Strap leaves and tall branched stalks with curved tubular paw flowers.
Branching leafy habit and hanging fruit trusses.
Related crop families share organ construction but retain distinct leaf and harvest forms.

art_decisions: Independent young rosettes, fans and reduced branched stems before flowering.
Curved leaf surfaces with tissue UVs and species-specific compound, palmate, peltate or strap anatomy.
Every flower, bud and harvest mesh stores its own attachment; biological proportions adjusted to existing game dimensions.
Fine structures use sparse opaque geometry; shader and quality settings remain unchanged.
Winter jasmine retains sparse trifoliate foliage on arching stems and solitary six-lobed flowers.
Queen of Night tulips have two alternating whorls of three tepals.
Maize ears carry wrapping husks and silk; brassicas retain their stalks and attached harvest organs.
